One user finds searching HN through Google gives better results than the Algolia-powered HN search. Searching "ml" in Algolia returns years-old, less relevant results, while Google surfaces more recent threads.

A user finds the HN search interface useful, especially the drop-down for choosing how results are sorted. Google does more black-box magic, whereas Algolia behaves as a faithful, predictable search engine.
A user says Algolia doesn't seem great for HN. Lately it sometimes fails to load results or is quite slow compared to Google Search. Another user reports encountering the same problem.
Workaround: a user tends to get better results with `query site:news.ycombinator.com` on Google than with the built-in Algolia search.

Their DocSearch program for open source projects is really great; the Jekyll docs' instant results usually find just what you want. The user's only complaint is wanting a plug-and-play solution deployable for private internal documentation sites.
Algolia has great analytics: you can tie a query to a purchase and analyze business value from real search queries. It's powerful and doesn't require exceptional engineering talent to use.
A user with startup and large ecommerce experience doubts the value proposition. Judging Algolia's accuracy on your own queries would require the same ML staff you hoped to avoid hiring.

A user has used Algolia for small sites and large enterprise clients (10B+) and always felt they got way more than they paid for. They can't think of another SaaS with such a smooth onboarding and retention ecosystem.
If you've ever tried installing ElasticSearch and then switched to Algolia, you'll understand how great a product it is.

A user says Algolia is easy to use and set up, but they switched to Elasticsearch over price and the closed-source license. Algolia is great to get started but doesn't make sense at scale; large indexes are just too expensive.
A user's team moved to Algolia mainly because of speed. Elastic Search and Solr could not compete.
A user running Algolia on their docs site is really happy with the service and ease of implementation. However, slow-loading pages sometimes cause the crawler to time out and miss content.
Using it for a side project, a user is very impressed with the developer experience. The React InstantSearch plugin is great and easy to add, and the documentation and admin UI are great.
A team A/B testing Typesense and Algolia is tempted to choose Typesense on pricing alone. They call Algolia's price-per-search model a little ridiculous for UIs with live search.

Facebook's open source sites (React, GraphQL, Yarn) use the free version. You include a JS file and an input and it just works. It has required zero maintenance, hasn't gone down, and the API hasn't changed.

A user searches users by name, bio and phone with Algolia, React Native and Firebase. Linking the two took a single Firebase cloud function. Typo tolerance alone makes it the best third-party search service in their view.
On Adafruit's Algolia-powered search, results start strong but quickly fall off into partial gibberish. Searching "lipo", by the end of page 1 only about every other result is relevant.

A team uses Algolia for a database of about 1.5M US nonprofits. Search is blazing fast and customizable, handles typos, alternate names, EINs and locations, and support has been very helpful. Their only complaint is that pricing is a bit steep.

A user calls Algolia a joy to use but says it's easy to exceed record limits. Every sort option requires a duplicate index, which turned their 30K records into 150K and forced them to build something custom.
A user misses the old HN search. The new one lacks basic operators like "ai OR artificial intelligence OR deeplearning" queries.
